items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Next is your first recording that you made for Japan, but in New York, with Terumasa Hino, by 1970, Journey to Air. ... We’re all in the studio together.

ctx.x: happened to him. He became a nut. I don’t know. Something happened to this guy. He was a Bud Powell kind of – he was a bebopper who went free, as a lot of those Scandinavian – that thing up there. It’s different, as I learned. Everytime I played the Fasching, in Stockholm, the guy in charge would say, “Lars would love to talk.” I talked to him. I could see his voice. I think he had a stroke. I think he had trouble, because for years – he lives alone, and he’s like, “Dave, I remember the great days,” like that.…
Next is your first recording that you made for Japan, but in New York, with Terumasa Hino, by 1970, Journey to Air.
That’s one of – that’s Hino getting – that’s Ascension. That’s Hino with whomever. Do they have the list of characters?
